title: The jobs gap in India’s growth story
lede: This year, five countries — Jordan, Micronesia, the Philippines, Sri Lanka and Vietnam — have moved up to the upper-middle income category as per the World Bank. Of these, Vietnam’s case is instructive. In 2009, it crossed the threshold for lower-middle income status, meaning it took the country 16 years to move up the income classification. India, which entered the lower-middle income group in 2007, remains stuck in that category, 19 years later. China’s ascent was even faster, reaching upper-middle income status in 2010, just 13 years after being classified as lower-middle income.

political.rationale: Critiques the prevailing narrative around India's economic growth by highlighting structural stagnation in the lower-middle-income bracket and contrasting it unfavourably with peer economies like Vietnam and China to spotlight the jobs and income gap.
